While it has been improved, this game still [b]fails to justify itself as a standalone game that costs just as much as DRG[/b]. It's not like it isn't enjoyable, but most of what's enjoyable about it is the enjoyable stuff that was already present in regular old DRG, and it lacks the replay value or longevity of DRG once you're done unlocking stuff.

[b]The attempt at rogue-like elements adds very little to DRG's formula[/b], at least in the way it was done here. For one thing, for being called "Rogue" Core, and being billed as a roguelite, it's barely any more Rogue-like than DRG already was (and DRG is certainly not a rogueli(ke/te)); the most meaningful "Rogue-like" elements present in Rogue Core are procedurally generated levels, and having to start the mission over, probably with a new seed, if you die. These are both already features of DRG. You might say that the level generation is a little more Rogue-like in Rogue Core because there are distinct floors, but this just doesn't bring much to the table other than the missions being longer. The change to the formula otherwise to make it a "roguelite" is only to add "pick from 4 upgrades" screens (which is really Slay the Spire/Survivors mechanics, and largely unrelated to Rogue-like design, despite the current trend of calling a game a "roguelike" when you really mean "deckbuilder"), and to randomize your starting loadout, which doesn't really make it any more or less rogue-like considering that even pure, traditional roguelikes have consistent starting gear for each class. And there's a good reason that those games have you start with certain gear and attributes and try to build into what your character is good at rather than picking up anything you see, instead of being purely games of grabbing every random thing you see with no build agency.
It doesn't bring any of the things that are interesting about roguelikes or roguelites to DRG, and it doesn't really bring anything interesting to the table in general, but rather, mainly just amounts to having a less interesting kit even at the end of a run than any character in DRG can have to start with. After all, the classes in DRG have more thoughtful kits with planned out synergy, while in Rogue Core you just have a grab bag of ♥♥♥♥. The randomization of elements that were symbiotic in DRG also means there is much less class interaction because you can't count on it, contributing again to it being a less interesting DRG (quite a shame because DRG had a successful co-op formula, which is not an easy thing to create, and with this game threw it out). And the game is easy enough that developing a well synergized kit is just not necessary to win. In fact, it's hardly necessary to engage with the expenite upgrades or kit RNG at all to win, because the most consistent strategy is just using the guaranteed resources in every level, the workbenches and bio-boosters, for upgrading your characters' innate abilities. Your Slicer doesn't really need to worry about whether his gun can kill the boss quickly when his slice ability has 5 stacks of eclipse system and 5 damage upgrades, Falconer scarcely needs to worry about her guns or ammo when she can easily be upgraded so that you can just mindlessly keep sending out the attack drone to shred everything on your behalf, Guardian isn't worried about getting hit when he can constantly spam fear effects (a strategy so broken that even players of modded difficulties don't run the fear mod on the coil gun in DRG because it trivializes the game so much), and so on. Which brings me to my next point:
[b]The game very quickly becomes completely rote.[/b] Rush workbenches and bio boosters, take whatever grab bag of expenite upgrades you roll, and unless you skipped all the work benches and got completely terrible RNG, shred the boss's health bar in like 5 seconds every phase. 

I thought before release that it would be nice if they were leaning more into the movement shooter aspects of DRG. That even does seem to be how it's billed. Technically a lot of actions are faster at base (although many cancels have been significantly nerfed, so it's debatable if you're truly faster than you can be in DRG), and the Reclaimers are presented as elites who are more combat-ready than the mining crews of regular DRG. But in practice I find that the game often feels slower and less responsive. Only one class, Slicer, has a traversal ability as part of its base kit. Using a pickaxe halts your speed and momentum. Falling causes you to be locked into an obnoxious, lengthy landing animation, making Cushion IV mandatory on everyone except maybe Slicer because the fall height to trigger this is aggravatingly low. I hardly get the impression that the Reclaimers are as elite or combat-ready as the game tells me when I remember that every member of the supposedly weaker mining crews of regular DRG has access to Dash. The way the "Q" press state for using class abilities work is also pretty unresponsive and clunky.

According to GSG this game started out as a new game mode for DRG. Had it only been that, I think it would just be inoffensive and a neat little diversion, if perhaps a very uneconomical and bloated addition to the game. But as a standalone game that costs as much as the main game it doesn't pull its own weight, or really offer any positive qualities not already offered by DRG.

This game is fun!  I've made my way through most of the available content, ascended three of my classes, and reclaimed a depth 4 facility.  Update 1 made this much more accessible; ammo is no longer a very scarce resource and missions can be done at a reduced pace.  The corespawn still hit like a hammer, and I've failed more runs than I've succeeded.

Random multiplayer is a bit harder than it is with DRG, even now when a lot of active players have gotten the hang of missions.  I think this is more of a play-with-friends-on-discord game than a play-with-random-strangers game.  I have yet to share a beer with randoms at Omega's Bar and Fitness, for example.  My partner still finds the combat much more difficult than hazard 4 DRG gameplay, she hasn't played more than 2 runs.

For future updates, I'm hoping for more intel objectives, more enemy types, more traversal tools, more endgame content (something to do with merits?), CRSPR flamethrower, and the Ossuary Depths.  I also hope they port some  of these tweaks (like auto-sprinting and faster ziplines) back to DRG.

There are only two mission types, but both of them are better than any of the mission types from DRG 1. Also, the new classes are badass.
Tell Omega that I will, respectfully, keep pressing the button.

I found it stupid that you cannot share perks in a COOP roguelike game, where choosing a perk would make either your build great or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. As a huge drg fan and someone who played in the closed alpha, this game is in a very rough state right now, and we had the first update recently and its still not there yet, however there are still things yet to be added and changes so by then i might change my review when its in a better state.

The problem is that the gameplay loop is pretty shallow and for me that's mainly the fault of two features:

Firstly the upgrade perks are still basic or boring and the ones that are unique needs you to gamble on hopefully getting other upgrades that synergize with it (a lot of upgrades are does [x] if you kill enemies with [y] element), so you end up doing basically the same build every run.

Secondly is the lack of different mission objectives, the only one is activating the elevator (hopefully for now) and the only thing that is different each run is what boss you will fight and what mini side objectives you will get, and you will most likely already experience all of them in like 10 hours of gameplay.

And for performance it runs well, but i have a good pc so i dont know how well it would run on something less powerful, but i do get some stutters rarely and got a few game crashes, but most likely due to the game still being in early access.

★ Now for the good stuff:

Each class is great with their own unique abilities, but some need a little more tuning up or reworks as they are not that fun to play (*cough* guardian), but what we got now are each fun in their own ways.

The weapons are great and are probably the best aspect of this game right now, even weapons returning from drg are fun to use with the different upgrades you could get for them.

In conclusion if you like drg you probably would like some aspect of this game, but for now its very shallow with not that much variety going, eventually each run will start feeling the same.

Im sure much of these things will get addressed and get better, thats the point of going into early access, and i feel this game has some potential to be as great as it good old brother, but for now i wont recommend this game and say hold on into you money as its not worth the asking price right now.

Deep Rock Galactic: Rogue Core looks familiar at first glance. The caves, the dwarves, the equipment and the general atmosphere all carry the DNA of the original Deep Rock Galactic.

Once the mission starts, however, it quickly becomes clear that this is a very different game.

Build choices, upgrades and a fair amount of luck play a much larger role here, and teamwork matters far more than in its predecessor. A good team can make a difficult run feel manageable, while a poor combination of builds or a lack of coordination can turn things into a rather expensive mining expedition.

Playing solo is possible, but significantly harder. Maybe some players will have an easier time with it, but for me the difference between solo and cooperative play feels enormous. Finding friends to play with or joining random players is often the better option, provided everyone is willing to work together rather than simply share oxygen in the same cave.

At least navigation is rarely the problem this time. The game is fairly linear and following the route forward is usually straightforward. The real pressure comes from the clock constantly pushing you onward.

Being in Early Access, balance is still moving around quite a bit. Some updates make the game feel brutally difficult, while others swing in the opposite direction and make runs surprisingly forgiving. Its long-term health will depend heavily on how Ghost Ship continues refining that balance over time.

I can recommend it, but with some caution. The foundations are solid and there is plenty of potential here, yet Rogue Core still feels a little green around the edges.

And if you plan to go in alone, be prepared for a rougher experience. At least for me, the caves seem to have very little sympathy for solitary dwarves.

Ideally, when you get powerups and better weapons, you feel more powerful. But the weapons are too weak, the enemies do too much damage, the missions are too long, the mining feels like crap, there's no meaningful rewards or progression (whoopdeedoo, 5% extra healing from red sugar, meanwhile there's 50 aliens biting my ass), the list goes on. Did you roll two crap guns? Oh well, better start the run over or settle in for 45 minutes of pain before you get inevitably bum rushed by 100 super powered aliens that can melee you through platforms and stick to you while you sprint and jump so they can keep meleeing you at all times. Even unlocking a beer to drink on the spaceship feels like a stupid waste of time doing a worthless and overtuned workout minigame. Allow me to get it out of the way before I continue: Rogue Core is NOT Deep Rock Galactic, at least not in the traditional sense you're thinking. Are you a dwarf? Are you going to shoot a bunch of aliens? Will you rock and stone? Yes!! However....

You will NOT be mining for minerals except for Expenite. You can't call in drops for ammo, those must be found in the environment. You will not always get the gun you want. Yes, that means you. You know I'm talking about you. HOWEVER each level contains a workbench that lets you buff your weapon to the point where it might actually become your favorite by the end.

You should also be aware that the fastest match I've been able to pull off was right at around 30ish minutes. YMMV, but guarantee expect it to take 30-60 minutes guaranteed depending on how many floors there are. 

Be also prepared to work your ass off and lose everything because of a party wipe. You will find that some matches suck and you just lose due to bad luck.

Is this game going to become the next Deep Rock Galactic? or Deep Rock Galactic 2? No.
Is this game fun where it it stands right now as an early access title? Surprisingly yes! 
Is this game worthy of the Deep Rock family of games? yes!!

Ghost Ship Games listening to their players and backtracking the way their systems worked in game has been a positive boon. Rogue Core has the potential to become the perfect FPS Rogue-like out on the market. It needs some polishing, definitely needs some bug fixing and some quality of life improvements, and that is ok. This title is early access, and if you temper your expectations just a smidge, you will find a gem of a game under the "construction" sign. 

My only critique at the moment is that Solo play is only viable to depth lvl 2. Depths 3+ get too difficult to play solo. Maybe the depth levels need to be explained better as a difficulty modifier. 

For newbies or solo players.... play guardian. it is the easiest class to play solo and all the class skills work in your favor running solo. Take advantage of his stun attack!!!!

The biggest problem for me is the constant interruptions. Every few minutes, you and everyone else must pick a perk, and then you have to wait for the others to finish. You just cannot get into a flow because there are way too many interruptions.On top of that, they force you to play as ugly female dwarves.The only solution from my point of view: shift the perk-picking mainly to the elevator ride and get rid of the ugly female dwarves... please!

The current reviews make no sense. Sounds like a bunch of people who bought this expecting it to be exactly like DRG. Maybe they just don't know what a rogue lite is. Or expected them to just asset flip the entirety of DRG.

Despite the initial criticism the game underwent, the following update 1 confirmed that GSG is on the right track with this game: if on the original version every run felt samey, there's already a lot more nuance and variance in every mission thanks to enhancements expansion and balance: the revised elemental damage system is particularly interesting and I hope it gets further built upon, and the new weapons and abilities feel right at home with the original ones from DRG.
I really hope GSG will continue to work on RC without getting discouraged from the initial backlash: I'm sure they'll deliver.
If you liked the og DRG, but the early access left you with a not so good impression, I highly suggest to keep an eye on the development and give this one a second chance down the road.

I have around 1,000 hours in the original Deep Rock Galactic on another Steam account. I played on the highest difficulties, both solo and with other players, so I know what I like about DRG and what I expect from a game in this universe.

I had around 28 hours in the Rogue Core playtest and alpha version. I played it before release, including a test about six months before launch. In the release version, I played for about 1 hour and refunded the game, because I quickly realized that it was almost the same thing I had already seen in the alpha.

Yes, the developers added some visual improvements. The station looks better, there are more details, and the game looks a bit more polished. But I care about the gameplay, not the station. And the gameplay still feels boring, repetitive, and weak.

Rogue Core tries to be a roguelike, but it does not have enough real variety. The perks are not interesting. They do not feel strong or meaningful, and they do not make me want to try different builds. After a few runs, everything starts to feel the same. Similar rooms, similar fights, similar pacing, similar missions. There is procedural generation, but it does not make the game feel fresh.

This is especially disappointing when compared to the original Deep Rock Galactic. The original DRG feels more varied, more alive, and much more fun to replay. It has better biomes, more memorable situations, and more reasons to come back. Rogue Core is supposed to be a new game in the DRG universe, but right now it feels smaller, weaker, and less interesting.

The price makes it worse. Asking around 30 dollars for the game in its current state feels too much. What makes it even stranger is that during the Steam Summer Sale 2026, the developers did not offer any discount at all. Even a small discount would have shown that they understand the current state of the game and want more players to try it and give feedback. But there was no discount.

The only positive thing I can mention is the cooperative player base. The people I played with mostly knew what they were doing. But I think this is because the active player base is small, so the people who still play are mostly the ones who already enjoy the game. The problem is that even with good teammates, I still did not have fun with the game itself.

I am very disappointed. The original Deep Rock Galactic was one of my favorite games, and I spent more time in it than in almost any other game. Rogue Core does not feel like a worthy next step for DRG. It feels like an expensive, unfinished, and repetitive experiment that was sold too early.

I do not recommend it in its current state. After 28 hours in the playtest and 1 hour in the release version, it is clear to me that the most important part, the gameplay, has barely changed. Maybe the game will become better after several major updates, but right now, for 30 dollars, it is a very weak offer.

After a bit of time with the playtest and now the EA release, I can firmly say this game is good. And the best part is that it will only get better.

Currently the game is lacking some of the around the edges polish and progression we've come to expect from a complete experience like base DRG or DRG: Survivor. I'm sure some more endgame content and metaprogression will come. So far the perkloadout and Bio-Booster deck provides a nice level of customisation while retaining the classic DRG class-based structure.

Rogue Core is a hell of a lot less forgiving than standard DRG. Even standard run still has you having to commit to putting some effort in because if you fall behind, like in any good roguelike, you start to really feel the pressure. The usual crew I play DRG with are all highly skilled at the game and those skills have transferred over well to Rogue Core. Unfortunately Rogue Core isn't a great place to start for new entrants to the series as it is far from beginner friendly.

Overall, if you love DRG and want to try something different that's a little more fast paced, give this game a go. You'll be supporting a studio that has put out some incredible games and board games over the last few years. I'm absolutely certain that GSG are going to build this game into another hallmark for the coop shooter genre. Thank you GSG, Rock and Stone!

Concept overall is great! It's not a bad game at all. But I would rank other rouge FPS titles alot higher than this. It definitely needs some refinements to the gameplay loop to make it more engaging. 

Dislikes: 
- ammo economy is too punishing. Let me shoot!!
- enemy count feels too few and too infrequent. There are far too many times of no action. I'd love to see enemy counts increase and damage/perk potency to increase as well.  
- powerups are too gradual. Each elevator success should grant increasing rewards.
- you never feel extremely overpowered like you do in other titles. When you create/roll a fantastic synergy build, it should feel extremely strong. Deadzone/abyssus for example you would wipe whole rooms in seconds. 
- Molly being renamed to Ellis seems like a crime! Dialogue sounding this is far inferior to Molly. 
- heavy weapons, equipment and artifact's are too infrequent. I'd love to see these tiered on every run. Equipment on level 2, heavy level 3 and artifact's on level 4. 
- a re-roll feature/veto feature that the team can vote for on all upgrade screens. It should cost exponite to re-roll. 
- movement speed and general mobility feels to slow. Each class having should have one of the following: a double jump, dash, faster sprint or hover/float. Etc. 
- Minimap feature. The terrain scan is great in the original, but feels really cumbersome and difficult to navigate in a faster paced rougelike. Keep the scanner, but give us a simple HUD or wrist mounted quick access map. 
- offensive ability tuning. Some classes can be built really well, others perform poorly. 
- glossary section explaining red, green and blue crit multiplies, status effects etc.
Rock, Stone, etc.

I am a huge fan of the original Deep Rock Galactic and of roguelites. Unfortunately, as it stands, I cannot recommend Rogue Core. It *can* be fun, but the upgrades are mostly really generic. Raw stat increases rather than something fun. Even the things that leave poison clouds or sticky flames where you move feel like they don't really do much. 

Customization is a little weird too in that the classes are locked to a specific gender. I'd love to play a Guardian woman, but unfortunately, I can't.

The things that excite me the most in this game are the weapons, and even then, it's mostly just the existing ones from DRG. So I could just be playing DRG instead, where the overclocks give me much more control to do fun builds instead of just raw stat upgrades.

I'm sure this will be a great game someday, but right now, I really can't recommend picking it up.

This game is not trying to be the exact same as DRG and is doing it's own thing as a coop roguelike, and I'd say that what it's doing is already very fun and really promising, especially since its only in early access and knowing Ghostship it can only go higher from here.

Reaperworms should not be invincible. I get wanting to overwhelm players if the timer runs out, but you should not make immortal enemies that one-shot you just because you decided to stay 30 more seconds than you should have. Bosses are bullet sponges that also deal way more damage than they should. Game is easier in solo somehow than with another player.
